GENERATE BURST BV2A-0_0 — Run C-9 Phase 2', BV2F pilot (barrow_v2 art site), barrow_v2 (art-first, sketch A), PILOT window cols 0-2 x rows 0-2: paint-over of the art blockout (BV2F Phase 2') panel 0_0 over a conductor LAYOUT GUIDE (Matt R-C9-185 and R-C9-188). task_id "BV2A-0_0".

IMAGE 1 is the canvas to EDIT (1536x1024): IMAGE 1 is not a flat-colour layout: it is a GREYBOX RENDER of a real 3D game level, seen from the game's fixed high three-quarter ORTHOGRAPHIC camera (53 degrees down), at true scale -- the small painted barbarian among the standing stones is 1.85 m tall. Every grey or coloured form is a real object that will be modelled at exactly this position and size. LIGHT WARM GREY ground = deep, smooth snow; the NARROW DARKER BROWN-GREY BAND = a trodden path through the snow, running up through the stones to the barrow door; PALE BLUE-GREY = the frozen mere, flat lapis-blue ice with pale cracks; the BRIGHT BLUE ribbon = a small frozen stream running down off the barrow's flank into the mere; the BROAD PALE TAN BAND along the water = a grey shingle beach under thin snow, with a thin line of drifted snow along it; the VERY PALE BLUE-WHITE ground = thick shore ice, its broken front (the pale striped edge) dropping to the sea; DARK SLATE-BLUE = the open winter sea, and the PALE FLAT DISCS on it = floating ice floes; MUTED GREEN-BROWN PATCHES = low dark juniper scrub and rust-brown winter heather poking through the snow; the SMALL GREY UPRIGHT SLABS around the path = a broken ring of carved standing stones (spiral and knotwork carvings on the faces turned toward the viewer), two of them FALLEN and lying in the snow, with a few lone standing stones further up the slope; the LARGE PALE DOME at the top = the barrow mound, earth and dead grass under thin snow; set into its front, a grey carved stone facade with a monumental lintel and posts around a DARK doorway -- the barrow's one great door; the BROWN WOODEN HULL heeled over at the left = an old longship wreck frozen into the shore ice, its broken ribs and timbers strewn across the shingle; the GREY CRAGGY MASSES = weathered granite crags and boulders with snow on their ledges; along the bottom, the GREY LAYERED WALL = sheer sea cliffs of layered granite under a snowy cliff top, with a DARK opening in the cliff foot = a sea cave, and a straight flight of rock-cut STEPS climbing the cliff face beside it from a flat natural rock shelf above the water; at the right, the large BROWN TIMBER building = a half-burned longhall of weathered grey-brown timber with one great DARK door; the BLACK-BROWN tangle beside it = the charred, collapsed gable of a burned building; the FLAT DARKER GREY ground around them = a yard of trampled ash and soot; the rows of thin BROWN POSTS = a broken wooden palisade; the long brown cylinders = fallen logs.
Use image_gen in EDIT mode on IMAGE 1 and paint over the greybox render, turning every grey form into what it stands for, in place. Paint OVER the render: every object keeps EXACTLY its silhouette, position and size (the 3D models are placed from this same layout, so anything moved will not match); shadows stay where the render puts them (one winter sun from the upper LEFT, 55 degrees up, short soft blue-violet shadows touching their objects). Paint the barbarian OUT -- he is there only for scale; leave open snow where he stands. Keep the stone ring's centre, the path, the barrow door's approach and the mere OPEN: no new rocks, trees or drifts on them. Small scatter is welcome only inside the scrub patches and at the foot of rocks and stones. One thin warm dark-brown ink line on every contour, the SAME weight everywhere. Palette and hand of IMAGE 2 (the approved Frost King's Barrow concept): cold blue-white snow, warm grey granite, rust heather, dark juniper, lapis ice, dark slate-blue sea with pale floes, grey shingle, weathered grey-brown timber, soot-black charred timber and ash; watercolour washes with pen detail. No sky, no horizon, no text, UI, border or characters.

THIS PANEL (0_0), from the render's own object map: the frozen mere (bottom right); thick shore ice (middle left); the shingle beach (centre); juniper and heather patches (top right); open snow (top right); 1 granite crag (bottom left). It has NO dark opening: paint no door, cave, hole or passage anywhere in it. Nothing else stands here: no other building, ship, standing stone, crag or cliff.

One image_gen EDIT call. ONE retry only if a painted strip was altered, a join remains, anything appears that the guide does not put there (an extra landmark, fire, river or any town), the small barbarian is still there, an object has moved off its greybox silhouette, or greybox areas remain unpainted — name the reason. Copy the output to out/BV2A-0_0.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "BV2A-0_0"; images = the file with prompt, references and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — the canvas to EDIT (painted neighbour strips + layout guide)
IMAGE 2 — the APPROVED Frost King's Barrow concept (Matt's pick): palette, light, snow, stone carving and painted hand ONLY -- NOT its layout
